title: Your Taxes panel
description: The /taxes page: a like-for-like Village of Pelham vs Pelham Manor comparison, a bar visual of how a property tax bill divides between governing bodies, a labelled list for the shares with no source (county, town), and explainer blocks describing what each body's share funds. Created because generateTaxSection had no data source — the bar widths, percentage labels and explainer copy existed only as markup and appeared in no JSON file. Prose fields accept the safe HTML subset and {{fact:<id>}} tokens.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema file.

note.description: The caveat block under the bars. Carries the sourcing state of each share — which percentages are confirmed, which are not.

comparison.description: Side-by-side village comparison at the top of the page. Each amount is rendered from its fact, and the bar lengths are computed from the facts' numeric values — so unlike bars[].bar_width they ARE proportional to the data.

title.description: Heading, e.g. 'Village of Pelham vs Village of Pelham Manor'.

subtitle.description: The basis of the comparison — the shared assessed value. A comparison without it is not like-for-like.

note.description: Caveat and source under the comparison.

fact_ref.description: facts.json id. Its numeric `value` sizes the bar and its `display` is printed. Build fails on an unknown id or a non-numeric value.

unverified.description: Shares with no published source, listed rather than drawn as bars so no bar width can be mistaken for a figure.

note.description: Where a resident gets a real number instead — their own bill and the Receiver of Taxes.

text.description: What is and is not known about this share.

bars.description: DISPLAY ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER, largest share first.

explainers.description: DISPLAY ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER. Deliberately a different order from `bars` — the pre-refactor page listed the bars as school/village/county/town but the explainers as school/county/village/town. Kept as two independent arrays rather than forced into one order.

learn_more.description: Outbound reading at the foot of the page, for readers who want the primary source rather than this site's summary of it. Rendered last.

label.description: Link text. Say what the reader gets, not just the publisher.

url.description: Destination. External, so it opens in a new tab.

note.description: Short line under the link naming the source.

label.description: Row name as printed, without the icon.

percent_text.description: The text printed at the right of the row — NOT a number, because most shares are not published figures. Real values include 'largest share*', '~25% ✓' and 'share not published'. Keep the hedging: only the Village of Pelham share has a source.

detail.description: Optional second line under the row name — the body's dollar figure where there is one. Safe HTML subset plus {{fact:<id>}} tokens.

bar_width.description: PRESENTATION ONLY — the CSS width percentage of the filled bar. This is NOT data and must never be read back as a tax percentage. Only the Village of Pelham width (25) corresponds to a sourced number; the school width is an illustrative proportion. Null draws an empty track, for a body whose share has no published figure: the row stays in the list without a fill that would read as a number. County and town moved out of the bars into `unverified` for the same reason. If a genuine published breakdown ever exists, add it as facts and render percent_text from those, but keep this field separate.

fill_style.description: Bar colour; renders as CSS class .bar-<value>. Must match an existing rule in the stylesheet.

governing_body.description: Foreign key to bodies.json id. Null for a row covering more than one body.

description.description: What this body's share of the bill actually funds. Safe HTML subset plus {{fact:<id>}} tokens — write {{fact:village-budget-fy2627}}, never a literal dollar figure.

accent.description: Block accent colour; renders as CSS class .<value> on .tax-explainer-block ('none' emits no extra class). Presentation only, and deliberately not aligned to the bar colours — the pre-refactor page used a different colour per block than per bar.

link.description: The source link at the foot of the block.
